title: Kinetic-Molecular Model of an Ideal Gas
topicTitle: Kinetic-molecular model of an ideal gas
notes: **Postulates:** (1) gas consists of a large number of identical molecules in random motion, (2) molecular volume is negligible compared to container volume, (3) no intermolecular forces except during collisions, (4) collisions are perfectly elastic, (5) collision duration is negligible compared to time between collisions.
**Pressure origin:** pressure arises from molecules colliding with the container walls. Each collision delivers a tiny impulse; the average over many molecules gives measurable pressure.

**Temperature and kinetic energy:** the average translational kinetic energy per molecule is $\langle K \rangle = \frac{3}{2}k_BT$. Temperature is a direct measure of average molecular kinetic energy.
**Why temperature cannot be negative:** kinetic energy is always positive, so absolute temperature $T$ must be $\geq 0$.
